sentences.text: Mononykus was a tiny theropod dinosaur that grew to between 1 and 1.2 meters long and weighed 3.5 kilograms.
This runner had a single clawed finger on each hand and stout forearms featuring a large claw measuring 7.5 centimeters.
Its body included fused wrist bones like modern birds and a keeled breastbone, while soft feathers likely offered insulation.
Inner ear structures resemble those of barn owls, and longer tail feathers may have aided in courtship displays.
A small skull with pointed teeth suggests it hunted insects and small animals such as lizards and mammals.
In the documentary Prehistoric Planet, the creature is shown with a facial disk similar to owls and a long, sticky tongue.
The holotype specimen IGM N107/6 was collected in 1987 from the Bügiin Tsav locality in the Gobi Desert.
Perle and colleagues first briefly described the animal in 1993 before providing more detail in 1994.
A new specimen was referred to the genus by Sungjin Lee and colleagues in 2019.
In 2008, the Korea-Mongolia International Dinosaur Expedition found a specimen containing seven tail vertebrae and a partial hindlimb.
The function of the specialized arms is unknown, though some researchers propose they broke open termite mounds.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined 15 foot bones for stress fractures but found none.
Mononykus belongs to the family Alvarezsauridae and is part of the Coelurosauria group related to birds.
Advanced members of this family, including Mononykus, Parvicursor, and Shuvuuia, form the subfamily Mononykinae.
The name was originally Mononychus in 1993 but changed that same year because a beetle already held that name.
It lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Mongolia within the Nemegt Formation.
The animal existed during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, spanning from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
Many artistic reconstructions and museum skeletons labeled as Mononykus are actually based on the related genus Shuvuuia.
Researchers assigned specimen IGM 100/99 to Mononykus in 1993 but later expressed doubts in 1994; it was eventually reassigned to Parvicursor in 2008.
